_sources.12: TY2025 standard deduction, married filing jointly: base $31,500 (Rev. Proc. 2024-40 as adjusted by OBBBA, P.L. 119-21) PLUS the additional amount for age 65: both spouses are 65 or older at the end of 2025 (taxpayer born 1958-05-01, spouse born 1960-11-15; a taxpayer born before January 2, 1961 is considered 65 - Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), Standard Deduction, and the date is printed on the form). Additional amount per condition for a married taxpayer is $1,600 (Rev. Proc. 2024-40; IR-2024-273), and there are 2 conditions (taxpayer age, spouse age; neither is blind), so $31,500 + 2 x $1,600 = $34,700; Form 1040 line 12 (printed as 12e)
_sources.13b: Schedule 1-A (Form 1040) TY2025, Part V (enhanced deduction for seniors) -> line 38 -> Form 1040 line 13b: MAGI = AGI $200,000 (Schedule 1-A line 31; v1 takes MAGI = AGI); the line 32 threshold for married filing jointly is $150,000, so the line 33 excess is $50,000; line 34 = 6% of $50,000 = $3,000; line 35 (the PER-PERSON amount) = $6,000 - $3,000 = $3,000; both spouses have valid SSNs and were born before January 2, 1961, so lines 36a and 36b each take $3,000 and line 37 = $6,000. The phaseout is per person: the joint deduction is 2 x ($6,000 - $3,000) = $6,000, NOT $12,000 - $3,000. v1 implements Part V only, so line 38 = line 37

description: Married filing jointly; one W-2 ($200,000 wages, $25,000 withheld); identity block stored with both spouses age 65+ (DOBs 1958-05-01 and 1960-11-15, both born before January 2, 1961) with SSNs, neither blind. Line 12 = $31,500 base + 2 x $1,600 age additions = $34,700. The Schedule 1-A Part V enhanced deduction for seniors phases out per person at this MAGI: line 13b = 2 x ($6,000 - 6% x $50,000) = $6,000. Taxable income $159,300 is figured with the Tax Computation Worksheet. Money values below are integer cents.
